questions.question: Why must large food molecules like carbohydrates, proteins, and fats be broken down during digestion?
options: To allow them to be absorbed into the body
To convert them into water and carbon dioxide
To prevent them from entering the blood
To turn them into larger storage polymers

questions.question: What is the main role of the blood in relation to digested nutrients?
options: To break down nutrients into simpler elements
To transport absorbed nutrients around the body to where cells need them
To filter out and excrete unused nutrients directly from the body
To produce enzymes that help digest nutrients in the bloodstream

questions.question: By what process do some small nutrient molecules move from the digestive system into the blood?
options: Active filtration
Osmotic suction
Diffusion
Phagocytosis

questions.question: How is the lining of the small intestine adapted to increase the amount of nutrient absorption?
options: It is completely smooth to allow food to slide quickly
It has a very small surface area to concentrate nutrients
It is covered in microscopic folds called villi that increase the surface area
It has a thick, impermeable muscular wall that prevents leaks

questions.question: Which statement best describes the nature of bacteria?
options: All bacteria are pathogens that cause harmful diseases in humans
All bacteria are completely harmless and have no effect on other organisms
Some bacteria are pathogens that cause disease, but many are harmless or helpful
Bacteria are non-living particles that only become alive inside a host

questions.question: Where in the human body do helpful, beneficial bacteria live in large numbers to assist with digestion?
options: Inside the acid-filled stomach
Inside the digestive system
Within the salivary glands of the mouth
In the muscular walls of the oesophagus

questions.question: How do helpful bacteria inside our digestive system assist in digesting foods that we cannot digest on our own?
options: They physically chew the food particles into smaller pieces
They release enzymes that break down these foods
They absorb the food whole and destroy it inside their cells
They produce strong stomach acid to dissolve the food

questions.question: How do helpful bacteria in the digestive system help protect us against harmful pathogens?
options: They produce antibodies that destroy all foreign cells
They raise the temperature of the gut to kill harmful invaders
They compete against the pathogens for resources and space
They engulf the pathogens through phagocytosis

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a digestion type with its description and location?
options: Chemical digestion uses muscular churning to grind food in the mouth
Chemical digestion involves physically breaking down food and occurs only in the oesophagus
Mechanical digestion physically breaks food into smaller pieces, such as chewing in the mouth
Mechanical digestion involves chemical enzymes and occurs only in the large intestine

questions.question: What is the biological function of enzymes in the digestive system?
options: They act as structural components of cell walls
They act as catalysts to speed up the chemical digestion of food molecules
They store energy for later use by the body's cells
They transport oxygen to the digestive organs

questions.question: What are proteins broken down into during chemical digestion?
options: Fatty acids and glycerol
Starch and simple sugars
Amino acids
Carbon dioxide and water

questions.question: Which chemical reagent is commonly used to test for the presence of the large carbohydrate starch?
options: Biuret reagent
Iodine solution
Benedict's solution
Ethanol emulsion test

questions.question: Which reagent can be used to test for smaller sugar molecules, such as glucose, produced from the breakdown of starch?
options: Iodine solution
Biuret reagent
Benedict's solution
Acidified water

questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct order in which food moves through the major organs of the digestive system?
options: Mouth -> Stomach -> Oesophagus -> Large intestine -> Small intestine
Mouth -> Oesophagus -> Stomach -> Small intestine -> Large intestine
Oesophagus -> Mouth -> Stomach -> Large intestine -> Small intestine
Mouth -> Stomach -> Small intestine -> Oesophagus -> Large intestine

questions.question: What happens to food material that cannot be digested by the human body?
options: It is completely absorbed into the bloodstream to be filtered by the kidneys
It is converted into fat and stored under the skin
It is passed out of the body as faeces
It is breathed out through the lungs as carbon dioxide gas
